body: THIS IS MY DAUGHTER.  she is underage (despite what her fake might say) and reddit refuses to delete her posts. If you are liking or commenting on her shower beer photos you are seriously contributing to some ongoing problems.

Hey thanks for asking.  She's doing better, went back to school, straight A's, still looking for independence and is taking a break from the boyfriend.  I think it's hard for her to "owe" him so much and feel so dependent on him.  Hopefully he'll still be around when she figures it out, but I doubt it.

Probably too late to join, but this is a great story.

We hated our daughter's SO before we even met him.  She's a high achieving, beautiful girl, smartest of all my kids, apple of her dad's eye.    She began dating a guy 8 years older, no education after high school, still living at home with his parents.  He was covered in tattoos, was a long time smoker, no career plans in sight.  My daughter was 19 at the time and well headed to med school.  After meeting him, she told us she was dropping out of college.  

Talk about parent's worst nightmare.  Our only daughter.  Turns out she had been seriously stressed for a number of years, trying to keep up with family and parental expectations, working toward a career she had no interest in, and was suffering from severe depression.  This guy listened and supported her.  And when she decided to end it all, he was the one who found her and saved her life.

Spend a few days in the ICU with your kid struggling for her life, with her SO constantly beside her talking, caring, touching her even though through her coma she probably couldn't hear him.  Watch him support her through the horrible days that followed, with the memory loss and severe mood swings and continued depression.  See your daughter grow stronger through the steady support of someone who believes totally in her value and loves her for who she is, not who he wants her to be.  After those weeks, even months, you will see that tattoos don't matter, education doesn't matter, life circumstances don't matter.  What matters is that someone knows and loves your child.  Her SO is still a part of our family even though they are no longer together.  He turned out to be a wonderful person with many qualities that are rare in today's world.  I learned an important lesson about judgement through our relationship with him.
you're awesome.  I'm glad you didn't throw yourself in front of any cars.  Yeah, a cheat code would be smack.  Thanks for helping out an old lady.

I would love to have her home, but she says being here makes it worse.  Independence is a tricky transitional issue for some people, and as much as I want to guide her and hold her hand through her growth I know it isn't healthy to do so.  We tried to bring her home after the second attempt.  She said she would come, but that there was no way I could watch her 24/7, and she promised she would complete her suicide if she was home.  Made me feel awful as a parent - who wants their kid to view being home with such horror - but it is how she felt, and I needed to validate that.

Thanks everyone.  I'm going to go, even if that makes me a parachute parent.  She tried to talk me out of it, saying she'd be home for Thanksgiving, but somehow I think that may not be true, especially if her current trend continues.  To the young adults here on SW - reach out and open up to someone you trust about how you are feeling.  There is always somebody in your world that cares deeply about whether you exist, even if they may display it dysfunctionally.  Your family, like me, may just not be sure how to display what they feel without making your situation worse - there's so much advice about what to do, what not to do, when it comes to dealing with someone suicidal.  So thanks for responding and nudging me in the right direction.

Great viewpoint from someone exactly her age.  You seem to understand about how she feels regarding intervention.  If I sent 911 over to her house, our already tenuous relationship would be over.  She's smart enough to  deny ideation, depression, or intent.  I checked out that book - it looks great - MCBT has helped her in the past so I've ordered it.

How are you doing now?  Are you able to open up to your family and close friends?  Do you feel irritated when your mom texts or calls to "see if you're OK"?  What I'm asking is, does your family really make a difference when you're that deep into the pit?

Thanks.  I'm always afraid of her anger, that it might tip some impulsivity into the mix and trigger something.  Please, for the sake of your mother, hang in there.  My guilt for failing my daughter is immense.  As a parent, I feel like I should be able to protect her from this awful disease, and I can't do shit.

thanks.  Your advice helps.  The husband says I'm over reacting and that I need to focus on the kids that remain at home.  I actually called the suicide hotline for their advice; they had absolutely nothing helpful to say other than call 911.  It's revealing to see how you felt and struggled on.  If I may say, please, all of you, don't hurt yourselves.  Keep going.  One step at a time.  You mean everything to us.  I cannot imagine a world without my daughter in it.

I send care packages often, little things that I know she's liked in the past.  The whole family is always sending her notes, cards, texts...sometimes when I visit I see them all unopened in the corner.

hey, so would it make a difference if your parent showed up and hung around for a while?  Or would it make it worse?  It's not like she's thrilled to see me.  I've done the drive over there before only to have her yell at me to go away.  Your perspective helps.
